claim: TDD prevents polluted LLM context by testing after each small step; batched changes cause broken code to compound in model context
quote: accuracy drops off a cliff once the context goes beyond these limits

claim: AI-generated tests test implementation rather than intent, creating circular validation; AI almost never writes auth/injection security tests
quote: AI-generated tests tend to test the implementation rather than the intent—because they're derived from the same code they're supposed to validate

claim: TestPilot achieves 70.2% median statement coverage and 52.8% branch coverage on 1,684 npm API functions; 92.8% of tests have no more than 50% similarity with existing tests

claim: Simply saying 'use red/green TDD' is sufficient guidance for frontier models; test-first prevents agents from generating unused or non-functional code
quote: A significant risk with coding agents is that they might write code that doesn't work, or build code that is unnecessary and never gets used, or both

claim: Thoughtworks workshop found TDD prevents AI agents from writing tests that verify broken behavior—circular validation is eliminated when tests precede code
quote: TDD prevents a failure mode where agents write tests that verify broken behavior. When the tests exist before the code, agents cannot cheat

claim: 115-paper survey: prompt engineering dominates (89% of studies); iterative repair loops now standard; weak fault detection remains the main unresolved challenge
quote: prompt engineering accounts for 89% of the studies due to its flexibility; weak fault detection is a critical limitation

claim: METR RCT (n=16 experienced OSS devs, 246 real tasks, avg 2h): developers 19% slower with AI; predicted 24% speedup; still estimated +20% after completing tasks
quote: developers using AI tools took 19% longer to complete coding tasks compared to working without AI assistance

claim: CoverAgent and CoverUp have test oracles designed to pass — they actively filter out bug-revealing tests, making them unable to detect existing bugs
quote: tools have 'test oracles designed to pass,' which prevents them from finding bugs since bugs are only exposed by failing test cases

claim: Meta ACH: LLM-based mutation testing with 73% engineer acceptance rate, equivalence detector precision 0.79/recall 0.47 (improved to 0.95/0.96 with preprocessing)
quote: Privacy engineers accepted 73% of generated tests; 36% were deemed privacy-relevant

claim: GitHub Copilot RCT: developers completed HTTP server task 55.8% faster with Copilot vs control group
quote: completed the task 55.8% faster than the control group

claim: Qodo Cover: open-source CLI/CI tool that generates tests, validates each runs and passes, and increases coverage; autonomously contributed a PR accepted into HuggingFace timm
quote: An AI-Powered Tool for Automated Test Generation and Code Coverage Enhancement

claim: GitHub Copilot /tests without existing suite: 92.45% of tests are failing/broken/empty; with existing suite: 54.72% failing; tautological rate drops 35% to 5-10% with spec-driven workflow
quote: If tests are generated without an existing test suite in place, 92.45% of the tests are failing, broken, or empty tests

claim: Test-first prompting with CWE references forces threat modeling before generation and catches hallucinations; adding security constraints alongside functional criteria improves security coverage

claim: SDD inverts traditional workflow with three rigor levels (spec-first, spec-anchored, spec-as-source) and a decision framework for when SDD adds value over simpler approaches
quote: decision framework helping practitioners determine when SDD provides value and when simpler approaches suffice

claim: MuTAP: augmenting prompts with surviving mutants achieves 93.57% mutation score on synthetic buggy code, detecting 28% more defects than standard LLM test generation
